command_or_fixture: Read-only scratch probe: _memory_ranked over live fragile_file records, sorted by the Requirement 3 key versus by flagged-then-churn.
counterexample_or_failure_condition: apply_decay never attenuates fragile_file, so effective_confidence equals base confidence (0.6 to 0.95 here); the 0.6 records sort first whether flagged or not, and 27 flagged records exceed the 20 cap.
expected: 1u8q1 (73), 1u8q3 (66), 1u8q2 (57), 1u43m (54), 1vn0v (46), as the planning walk selected.
known_bad_detection_method: Probe on the live corpus showed the specified key yields a different batch than the planning walk.
limitations: Probe uses the current ranking internals, not the not-yet-written order parameter.
observed: Requirement 3 key top 5: 21rnt (flagged, churn 9), 1vrbp (flagged, churn 1), 1u25a, 1u2ju, 1v1ux (all unflagged, 0.6). Also churn has no numeric field; it exists only in the decay_basis string, and the 'one view field' named under Affected Architecture Docs is not defined by any requirement.
proposition: Requirement 3's weakest key (effective_confidence ascending first) applied to memory_search(kind='fragile_file', order='weakest', limit=5) returns the Requirement 2 fragile batch: the 5 flagged records with the highest target churn.
safety_and_authorization: Read-only; no repo or memory mutation.

disposition_rationale: Spec defect: define the fragile pass ordering (flagged first, churn descending, id) independent of effective confidence and name a numeric churn source, before implementation.

counterexample_or_failure_condition: fragile_file never attenuates from churn, so effective_confidence equals base confidence and dominates the key; low-confidence unflagged or low-churn records sort first.
expected: 1u8q1 (73), 1u8q3 (66), 1u8q2 (57), 1u43m (54), 1vn0v (46), matching the planning walk.
known_bad_detection_method: The spec's Requirement 3 key, applied to the live 175-record corpus, returned unflagged low-churn records instead of the planned top-churn flagged batch.
limitations: Readiness review of the plan; no implementation exists. Corpus state as of 2026-11-22.
observed: 21rnt (0.6, flagged, churn 9), 1vrbp (0.6, flagged, churn 1), 1u25a, 1u2ju, 1v1ux (0.6, unflagged). AC-4 can pass on an equal-confidence fixture while the real corpus diverges, and AC-6 with the shipped tool would not reproduce the planned batch.
proposition: Requirement 3's weakest sort key (effective_confidence first, flagged then churn as tie-breaks) applied with kind=fragile_file yields the Requirement 2 fragile pass: the 5 flagged fragile records with the highest churn.
public_path: memory_search(kind='fragile_file', order='weakest', limit=5) as specified in Requirement 3 and AC-4
safety_and_authorization: Read-only in-process calls; no repo or memory mutation.

disposition_rationale: Required AC-4/AC-6 and Requirement 2 contradict Requirement 3; fix the fragile pass key (needs_reverification filter, churn desc, memory_id) and give the AC-4 fixture unequal base confidences so the Requirement-3 key is a failing known-bad.

command_or_fixture: Read wf_server/memory_handlers.py (MEMORY_SEARCH_CAP=20 at line 48, n=min(limit, cap), no offset) and memory_records.apply_decay (created_ts basis); applied the planning walk keep ratio (7 of weakest 10, 4 of 5 fragile) to successive runs inside 30 days.
counterexample_or_failure_condition: The skip is applied only by the reviewer reading updated_at; queryless memory_search caps at MEMORY_SEARCH_CAP=20 with no offset, and decay is measured from created_at, so kept records stay at the top of the weakest order and fill the 20-record window.
expected: Each run within 30 days still yields a full batch of up to 15 unstamped records.
known_bad_detection_method: Cap arithmetic against the replacement promise shows the plan fails after two to three runs inside 30 days.
limitations: Arithmetic projection from the planning walk ratio, not an executed multi-run simulation; operator run cadence may be slower than 30 days, in which case the stall does not arise.
observed: Weakest pass: about 13 usable of 20 on run 2, about 6 on run 3, about 0 on run 4; fragile pass exhausts its window after about 4 runs. The re-stamp does stop re-picking the same kept records, but the replacement rule becomes unsatisfiable and the batch silently shrinks; no AC tests the skip (AC-5 pins only the stamp).
proposition: The keep re-stamp plus the 30-day skip lets repeated runs replace skipped records with the next record in the weakest ordering (Requirement 2), so repeated runs keep auditing new records.
public_path: memory_search(order='weakest') plus reviewer-side updated_at skip, per Requirements 2-4
safety_and_authorization: Read-only code reads and scratch arithmetic; no repo or memory mutation.

disposition_rationale: Simplest repair: have order='weakest' exclude records updated within 30 days (or one updated_before filter) so the tool applies the skip, and add an AC whose fixture stamps a weak record and asserts the next record takes its place, with the exclusion removed as the known-bad. Alternatively state in the seed that the batch may run short.

command_or_fixture: Code read of memory_handlers.memory_search_response and memory_records.apply_decay/reconcile_memory_record, applied to the spec's planning-walk outcome (11 keeps of 15).

known_bad_detection_method: Not executed: code-read trace from the reviewer's skip back to the tool cap and the created_at decay basis.
limitations: Arithmetic projection from the spec's planning-walk outcome; not executed across runs.

safety_and_authorization: Read-only; no repo or memory mutation.

artifact_or_test_id: 244fh Requirement 2, Requirement 3, AC-4; memory_records.py apply_decay fragile_file branch
command_or_fixture: memory_search(kind='fragile_file', status='active', limit=20) on the live corpus; grep Confidence: over fragile_file records; read memory_records.apply_decay lines 1709-1716
counterexample_or_failure_condition: fragile_file records never decay (memory_records.apply_decay sets only needs_reverification and decay_basis 'target_churn:N (flag only)'), so effective_confidence equals base confidence, which varies 0.6 to 0.95 across the corpus. Sorting by effective_confidence first returns the lowest base-confidence fragile records, flagged or not, ahead of the high-churn flagged ones.
expected: The five flagged fragile records with the highest churn (planning walk: 73, 66, 57, 54, 46) come first.
known_bad_detection_method: Shipped memory_search(kind='fragile_file', status='active', limit=20) showed the planning-walk records at effective_confidence 0.9-0.95 while the corpus holds fragile records at 0.6-0.85; the Requirement 3 key would rank those lower-confidence records first, refuting the spec claim.
limitations: No implementation exists yet; the defect is in the specified contract. Repair options: define the fragile pass key as flagged-first then churn descending (e.g. a separate order value or a kind-aware key), and state it so AC-4 and Requirement 3 agree.
observed: Those records carry effective_confidence 0.95/0.95/0.95/0.9/0.95 (e.g. 1u8q1 churn 73 eff 0.95). Corpus base confidences for fragile_file: five at 0.6, one 0.7, three 0.8, five 0.85. Under the Requirement 3 key the limit=5 call returns 0.6 records, none of the planning-walk five. AC-4's 'flagged before unflagged, higher churn first' contradicts Requirement 3 whenever confidences differ, and AC-6 must use the shipped tool.
proposition: Requirement 3's order='weakest' sort key (effective_confidence ascending first, then flagged-first, then churn descending) produces the fragile-file batch that Requirement 2, AC-4 and the planning walk describe.
public_path: memory_search(kind='fragile_file', order='weakest', limit=5) as Requirement 2 and AC-4 prescribe
safety_and_authorization: Read-only memory_search and file reads; no repo or memory mutation.

disposition_rationale: Blocking: the shipped tool as specified cannot produce the batch the seed step will tell reviewers to audit, and AC-4 is internally inconsistent with Requirement 3. A spec edit before readiness is cheapest.
